scenes.headline: Still on an iPhone XS or XR?
scenes.say: Still using an iPhone XS or XR? Update it. Right now.

scenes.headline: Apple patched a bug that may have been used in real attacks
scenes.say: On October twenty-sixth, Apple patched a CoreGraphics bug on older iPhones. Apple says it may have been exploited in real attacks.

scenes.headline: may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals
scenes.say: Apple's words: an extremely sophisticated attack, against specific targeted people.

scenes.headline: One booby-trapped file
scenes.body: Your phone processes a malicious file → attacker can run code on it.
scenes.say: One booby-trapped file, and an attacker can run code on your phone.

scenes.headline: Old iPhones waited ~4 weeks

items.text: US CISA lists it as a known exploited bug
iPhone XS, XS Max, XR finally patched

scenes.say: Here's the twist. Newer iPhones got this fix in late September. A day later, US agency CISA listed it as a known exploited bug. The older models waited about four more weeks.

scenes.headline: Old devices get fixes last.
scenes.body: Letting personal phones on your company network? Check the OS version at the door.
scenes.say: Analyst note: old devices get fixes last. If your company lets personal phones on its network, check the OS version at the door.

scenes.headline: Do this tonight
scenes.say: Tonight: Settings, General, Software Update. And turn on automatic updates.

scenes.headline: The security story behind the headline.
scenes.say: Sources are in the description. Follow Securidge.
